author: Robin E
title: The Isley Brothers receive star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, cementing a timeless legacy - NewsBreak
text:
By Robin E ,
1 hours ago Music legends The Isley Brothers Receive Hollywood Walk of Fame Star When it comes to iconic American music groups, only a select few have shaped the sound of multiple generations. While legends like The Temptations and The Jackson 5 helped define eras of soul and pop, The Isley Brothers stand apart for their unmatched longevity, adaptability, and influence across genres . This week, their contributions were formally etched into entertainment history.
On Wednesday morning, The Isley Brothers received the 2,834th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame . Marking a long-overdue recognition for one of the most influential groups in music history. The ceremony honored surviving brothers Ronald “Ronnie” Isley and Ernie Isley , whose careers span more than seven decades.
KTLA 5 entertainment anchor Melvin Robert emceed the celebration, which featured remarks from Jon Platt , chairman and CEO of Sony Music Publishing, and legendary producer and songwriter Terry Lewis , who praised the group’s impact on soul, R&B, funk, rock, and hip-hop.
Related Headlines
For fans and industry insiders alike, the moment symbolized not just success — but endurance.
From Gospel Roots to Global Influence The Isley Brothers originated in Cincinnati, Ohio , beginning their musical journey in 1954 as a gospel trio consisting of brothers O’Kelly Isley Jr., Rudolph Isley, and Ronald Isley . Early on, the group performed spiritual music until the tragic death of their younger brother Vernon Isley in 1955.
After relocating to New York City in the late 1950s, the group transitioned into secular music. A pivotal decision that would reshape American popular sound. Their breakthrough came in 1959 with the release of “Shout,” a raw, call-and-response anthem that became a cultural staple and sold over a million copies.
“Shout” didn’t just chart — it became a blueprint for live performance energy, influencing artists across rock, soul, and pop music for decades to come.
Reinvention Across Decades Throughout the 1960s, The Isley Brothers recorded for multiple labels, releasing hits like “Twist and Shout” and Motown’s “This Old Heart of Mine (Is Weak for You)” . But their most defining move came in 1969 , when they released “It’s Your Thing” on their own label, T-Neck Records .
The Grammy-winning song wasn’t just a hit — it was a declaration of artistic independence, predating conversations about artist ownership and creative control by decades.
In 1973 , the group evolved again, welcoming younger brothers Ernie Isley (lead guitar, drums) and Marvin Isley (bass), along with brother-in-law Chris Jasper (keyboards). This transformation turned The Isley Brothers from a vocal trio into a fully realized band, ushering in what many consider their golden era.
Albums That Defined R&B and Funk Throughout the 1970s and early 1980s, The Isley Brothers released a legendary run of albums, including:
3 + 3 The Heat Is On Between the Sheets The Heat Is On reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200 , while Between the Sheets became one of the most sampled albums in hip-hop history.
Though the six-member lineup split in 1983, the group’s legacy continued. Ronald and Ernie Isley later achieved renewed mainstream success in the 1990s and early 2000s with albums like:
Mission to Please (1996) Eternal (2001) Body Kiss (2003) The album Eternal spawned the hit “Contagious,” introducing the group to an entirely new generation of listeners.
As of 2026 , The Isley Brothers continue performing with Ronald and Ernie Isley carrying the torch.
Sampling, Hip-Hop, and Cross-Generational Impact Few groups can claim influence across six consecutive decades — but The Isley Brothers did just that.
Their music has been sampled and reimagined by some of hip-hop and R&B’s biggest names:
Ice Cube sampled “Footsteps in the Dark” for “It Was a Good Day” The Notorious B.I.G. used “Between the Sheets” for “Big Poppa” Aaliyah covered (At Your Best) You Are Love on her debut album Gwen Stefani sampled “Between the Sheets” on “Luxurious” In 2022 , the group collaborated with Beyoncé on Make Me Say It Again, Girl , proving their relevance remains intact even in the modern era.
Why the Hollywood Walk of Fame Still Matters for Music Legends While some critics argue that the Hollywood Walk of Fame has become overly commercialized, the honor still holds major cultural weight. Especially for legacy artists whose work predates streaming, social media, and viral fame. For acts like The Isley Brothers , the Walk of Fame represents institutional recognition from the entertainment indu stry itself, not just fan appreciation or chart success.
A star on Hollywood Boulevard places artists in permanent cultural conversation alongside legends from film, television, radio, and music. Unlike awards that can fade from memory, Walk of Fame stars are literal landmarks—visited daily by fans from around the world. For artists whose influence spans generations, the star becomes a physical marker of longevity and historical relevance.
In the case of The Isley Brothers, the honor acknowledges not just commercial success, but artistic endurance. Their catalog has remained relevant for more than 70 years. Continuously rediscovered by new audiences through sampling, covers, Verzuz moments, and collaborations with modern stars. Few groups in music history have managed to evolve while preserving their identity in the way the Isleys have.
A Legacy Still in Motion Even in recent years, Ronald and Ernie Isley have continued to perform, collaborate, and release new music. Proving that their artistry is not confined to the past. Their 2022 album Make Me Say It Again, Girl —featuring Beyoncé—served as a reminder that the group still commands respect from the highest tier of modern artists.
Their ability to remain culturally present while honoring their roots is a rare achievement. The Hollywood Walk of Fame star does not mark an ending. But rather a continuation of a legacy that refuses to fade.
With this honor, The Isley Brothers officially join a select group of music legends whose influence has transcended trends, formats, and generations. Their star on Hollywood Boulevard now stands as a permanent tribute to a group that helped define American music itself.
Honors That Match the Legacy The Hollywood Walk of Fame star joins a long list of prestigious honors already earned by the group, including:
Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction (1992) Hollywood Rockwalk (1997) Vocal Group Hall of Fame (2003) Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award (2014) In 2021, the group participated in a highly celebrated Verzuz battle with Earth, Wind & Fire , hosted by Steve Harvey. An event that highlighted their cultural reach and catalog depth.
Why the Hollywood Walk of Fame Still Matters While some critics view the Hollywood Walk of Fame as symbolic, its significance cannot be overstated. A star is not awarded lightly — recipients must demonstrate lasting cultural impact , not just commercial success.
For music legends like The Isley Brothers, the Walk of Fame serves as a permanent historical marker . Ensuring future generations understand who shaped the sound of American music.
Other legendary groups honored on Hollywood Boulevard include:
Boyz II Men The Temptations The Miracles Kool & The Gang By joining this elite list, The Isley Brothers are officially enshrined alongside peers who transformed the music industry.
A Legacy That Refuses to Fade With over 18 million units sold in the United States , multiple gold and platinum albums, and a Guinness World Record for charting hits across six decades, The Isley Brothers’ impact is undeniable.
Their Hollywood Walk of Fame star is more than recognition — it’s a reminder that true artistry transcends trends.
As Ronald and Ernie Isley stood on Hollywood Boulevard Wednesday morning, the moment symbolized something rare in music. A legacy built not on hype, but on consistency, innovation, and soul.
Few groups have shaped the past, present, and future of R&B the way The Isley Brothers have — and now, their names are literally written into history.
